history.dynasty: Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission (headquarters: Belur Math, Howrah, West Bengal; founded 1897 by Swami Vivekananda)
history.summary: FLAG - NOT A CONVENTIONAL TEMPLE: this row is an Ashrama - a monastic and service institution of the Ramakrishna Order - not a conventional Hindu temple. It does house a shrine/temple to Sri Ramakrishna where daily worship, bhajans and morning/evening aarti are held, but its primary character is a monastic centre with schools, medical and welfare services. Keep-or-drop decision needed for the temples dataset. The official belurmath.org centre page states this branch centre was started in 1937. It stands on Sebastian Bia Road (Nongkynrih), Laitumkhrah, Shillong 793003 (HWC2+F6C per place data; geocoder: 25.5712, 91.90053). Listed activities: an allopathic-cum-homeopathic dispensary with ayurveda and physiotherapy sections; a mobile medical unit treating patients in 70 villages; three units of Gadadhar Abhyudaya Prakalpa; a students' home for tribal boys; welfare activities (pecuniary, educational and medical aid); and celebration of Durga Puja. Its sub-centre, the Vivekananda Cultural Centre, stands on the very spot where the Quinton Memorial Hall stood, in which Swami Vivekananda delivered his last public lecture in April 1901; it runs a computer training centre, public library, drawing/painting and spoken-English classes, the Vivekananda Youth Forum and a trilingual online magazine 'Ka Jingshai - The Light'. Visitor accounts describe a serene, secluded campus with a guest house for devotees (donation-based boarding, book in advance by mail), simple vegetarian meals, a small museum on the Northeast and a library of Ramakrishna-Vivekananda literature; reviewers specifically praise the evening aarti at the Ramakrishna temple on the premises.

name: Ram Krishna Mission Ashrama
town_description: Shillong is the capital of Meghalaya in the East Khasi Hills district, a hill station at about 1,496 m known as the 'Scotland of the East'. It was the capital of undivided Assam until 1972 and remains the state's administrative, educational and cultural hub, with a predominantly Khasi tribal population alongside Bengali, Nepali, Assamese and other communities (verify). The ashrama stands in Laitumkhrah, a locality in eastern Shillong (verify).

travel.airport: Shillong (Umroi) Airport, approx. 25-30 km from the city (verify; limited scheduled services). Nearest major airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati, Assam (approx. 100-125 km by road; verify).
travel.railway: Guwahati railway station is the nearest major railhead (approx. 100 km by road; verify); onward by taxi or bus via NH-6.
travel.road: Shillong is well connected by road to Guwahati (approx. 3-4 hours via NH-6; verify); within the city, local taxis and shared cabs serve all localities (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather (verify). Durga Puja is the centre's major public celebration.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily bhajans and worship are held; morning and evening aarti are specifically praised by visitors (verify exact public visiting hours - the ashrama has not published them). The guest house is donation-based (reported ~Rs 500-600/person/day; verify) and primarily for devotees - book in advance by mail; guests are expected to be disciplined and self-servicing. Dress modestly.
